messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High percent packet loss reported from eu-north1 POP (cdn-eun1-01). Alerting on-edge->origin path loss > 10% for 5m. Impact: increased request errors and timeouts for EU-North region. Paging oncall.

alice (oncall): Ack — on it. I'm pulling metrics now and will start live triage. tagging @raj for net help.

alice (oncall): Dashboard snapshot: 5xx rate spiked to 7% (baseline <0.3%). RT p50 up ~120ms, p95 up ~600ms for eu-north1. CDN edge health shows decreased connectivity to origin via ISP-AS34567.

marta (sre): Seen concurrent alerts from synthetic checks hitting eu-north1 caches. Some customers report 502/504. ETA slack channel for customers: support team to prepare templated update.

kevin (support): Prep note for Support: "We are investigating intermittent request failures for EU-North. Engineers are triaging network and CDN routing. We'll update in 15m." Holding list of impacted customers and contact channels.

alice (oncall): Quick network probe from our edge into the origin:

```
# from edge-host-1
mtr -r -c 50 origin-eu.example.net

Host                      Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
1. 10.0.0.1                  0.0%    50    0.4   0.6   0.2   12.1   1.2
2. 203.0.113.5               0.0%    50    1.1   1.3   0.8    2.7   0.3
3. 198.51.100.9             18.0%    50  120.5 115.2   2.3  300.2  60.1
4. origin-eu.example.net    18.0%    50  121.0 116.0   3.1  301.0  59.6
```

alice (oncall): Looks like packet loss starts at hop 3 (upstream ISP/peer). This aligns with CDN provider telemetry.

raj (netlead): Confirming. I can open a BGP emergency route to prefer alternate provider path AS39876, and tell CDN to failover edge traffic to fallback-pop eu-west2 while we stabilize. Anyone object? :thinking:

marta (sre): +1 to reroute to fallback-pop. Need to watch latency impact to affected users but preferable to losing traffic.

fastcdn-support: We're seeing an anomalous route withdraw on our peering with AS34567 affecting eu-north1 -> origin reachability. Our infra team suggests two mitigations: 1) trigger CDN control-plane failover to alternate POP pool, 2) request customer-side BGP preference to alternate transit (if available). We can do failover immediately — ETA ~3m to start traffic shift.

alice (oncall): Action plan (summary):
- fastcdn to initiate POP failover to fallback pool (eu-west2 cache) — fastcdn-support
- raj to announce temporary BGP path to prefer AS39876 for origin reachability
- marta to watch canary traffic and error rates
- kevin to send interim customer message noting region degraded and mitigation in progress

ops-bot: Change note recorded: incident/1879001111 created by alice. Next update scheduled in 10m.

fastcdn-support: Starting failover now. Will progressively shift eu-north1 traffic to eu-west2 caches to avoid cache stampede. Monitoring.

alice (oncall): Raj, please post the exact BGP commands you plan to run so I can validate. Also lowering DNS TTL for cdn-edge.quickhosting.example from 300 -> 60 while we shift.

raj (netlead): Running prep command, will do a targeted prepend and local-pref change via our transit. Commands (example):

```
# net team (on our router fabric)
configure terminal
router bgp 65012
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map PREFER-AS39876 out
exit
```

Then apply route-map to raise local-pref for routes through AS39876. Will push in ~2m.

marta (sre): Noted. Watchlist: p95 latency, 5xx, origin-to-edge retransmits.

kevin (support): Customer update posted at 12:07 UTC: "We're seeing degraded performance in EU-North due to upstream network issue. Engineers are shifting traffic to alternate caches and monitoring. More updates shortly." (ticket IDs: #4532,#4533)

fastcdn-support: Failover in progress — initial shift 25% done. Error rate dropping at some edges. Continuing.

alice (oncall): BGP pref applied by raj. Confirmed our routers now prefer AS39876 path to origin. Observing immediate reduction in packet loss on edge -> origin path.

marta (sre): Metrics update: 5xx down from 7% -> 1.1% after partial shift; p95 decreased from 600ms -> 220ms for affected routes. Some user sessions affected will still experience errors but trending better.

fastcdn-support: Failover complete for eu-north1 traffic to fallback pool. CDN reports backend connectivity stabilized.

alice (oncall): Good. Kept TTL lowered to 60 for 30m. Support, please update customers that traffic is being served from fallback POP and most services restored; some cached content may be slightly stale until TTL expires.

kevin (support): Updated customers at 12:32 UTC. No escalations so far.

raj (netlead): Leaving a sticky route pref for 45m to ensure stability. Will coordinate with transit provider and ask AS34567 to confirm route restore. If AS34567 confirms healthy, we'll revert local-pref.

marta (sre): Starting post-incident monitoring window. Will collect traceroutes and CDN telemetry for RCA. Please attach any customer complained traces to this thread.

alice (oncall): Handoff to raj for network follow-up and fastcdn-support for RCA. I'm stepping off after 30m if stable. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

raj (netlead): Taking over as incident owner for next steps. Will liaise with AS34567 and fastcdn. Leaving notes: root-cause likely an upstream route flap/withdraw affecting a subset of paths to origin; mitigated by reroute and CDN failover. Final status will be updated after vendor RCA.

fastcdn-support: We will open an RCA ticket and share timeline. Observed a flapping route advertisement from AS34567 which caused the path to origin to intermittently drop. Provider rolled back change at 12:40 UTC.

marta (sre): Closing notes: user-facing impact limited to EU-North for ~33 minutes, majority traffic restored via fallback POP. Postmortem requested. Assigning to raj (network) + marta (sre) + fastcdn-support.
